summary: Remote WebSocket peer drives PTY shell, filesystem, and git operations on the installer's host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a WebSocket client whose server-sent messages are routed to a full remote-control surface on the machine running the agent. A `terminal_input` message writes attacker-supplied bytes directly into a PTY spawned via node-pty against `process.env.SHELL || 'bash'` (PowerShell/cmd on Windows), giving the remote peer an interactive shell. Other message handlers perform arbitrary file read/write/delete/move, git commit/push, and file transfer against the host workspace. An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to shell out to `npm install <pkg>@latest` and restart itself via a generated systemd/launchd/PM2/wscript upgrade script, letting the same remote peer force a re-pull and restart on demand. Whoever controls the WebSocket server has full-host code execution and filesystem/git write access on every installer running the agent; even though the update source is the public npm registry and the fixed package name, the control channel itself is the backdoor primitive.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
